title: Lock Upp 2 Contestant Sufi Motiwala Opens Up About Assault and Personal Loss After Eviction
excerpt: The 21-year-old content creator shared harrowing accounts of an alleged assault at a PG accommodation, his grandmother's death, and struggles with close relationships after leaving the Netflix reality show.
body:
• Sufi Motiwala revealed he was allegedly assaulted by a former roommate at a PG accommodation, an incident that left him locked in a bathroom for 12 hours.
  • The content creator shared that he missed his grandmother's final phone call two days before her death, and his family did not allow him to attend the funeral.
  • His grandmother left him Rs 50,000, which he used to buy a phone — a purchase that launched his career as a digital creator.
  • Motiwala also spoke about how developing romantic feelings for male friends during college led to a lasting fear of close relationships.

Content creator and reality television contestant Sufi Motiwala has shared a series of deeply personal revelations following his eviction from Lock Upp Season 2, the Netflix captive reality show hosted by Farah Khan and Riteish Deshmukh. The 21-year-old fashion commentator left viewers emotional with accounts of an alleged assault, family grief, and his struggle to form close bonds.

Alleged Assault at a PG Accommodation

Motiwala's most disturbing disclosure involved a former roommate at a paying guest accommodation. He described waking up repeatedly to find his roommate staring at him from across the room.

https://x.com/yespunjab/status/2081697814900531293

"My roommate would just be sitting on his bed and keep staring at me as I slept. That would make me really scared. One day, he just tried to force himself on me and started kissing me, making me extremely terrified."

— Sufi Motiwala, Lock Upp Season 2 contestant

After the incident, Motiwala said he ran downstairs and reported the assault to the PG owner, according to NDTV. The response, he claimed, was equally shocking: "The PG owner told me, 'Why are you sleeping with him? You should sleep with me.'" He said the encounter left him so traumatised that he locked himself inside a bathroom for nearly 12 hours.

A Grandmother's Final Call

Motiwala also spoke about the loss of his grandmother. She had called him two days before she died, but he missed the call. He learned of her death shortly after and said his family did not allow him to attend the funeral.

Before her passing, his grandmother had set aside Rs 50,000 for him. Motiwala used the money to buy a phone — a purchase he described as the starting point of his career as a content creator. That phone became the tool through which he built an Instagram following that has since crossed 370,000.

Fear of Forming Close Bonds

His third revelation centred on friendships and romantic feelings. During his college years in Delhi, Motiwala said he had only two close male friends. Over time, he developed romantic feelings for one of them, which altered the friendship and created distance between them. He admitted that the experience left him afraid of getting too close to people.

According to the show's episode records, Motiwala had previously revealed a related secret during the competition: that the first two times he formed a close bond with a male friend who made him feel safe, he fell in love with them and lost them both.

From Viral Reels to Reality Television

Born on October 9, 2004, Motiwala first gained attention through candid fashion commentary on Instagram, where his unfiltered "roasts" of celebrity outfits attracted a loyal Gen Z audience. He made his reality television debut on The Traitors in 2025, hosted by Karan Johar on Prime Video, before joining Lock Upp Season 2 this year.

During his time on the show, Motiwala clashed with fellow contestants including Shreya Kalra and Varun "Laila" Yadav, whom he accused of bullying. He also opened up about his coming out experience as a gay Muslim man, recalling how his 70-year-old grandmother told him, "At least try being bisexual. If you happen to like a girl, all our lives would be sorted out."

A Broader Conversation

Motiwala's disclosures have added to an ongoing conversation around Lock Upp 2 and LGBTQ+ representation on Indian reality television. Earlier episodes drew criticism after Ram Kapoor made remarks about being "scared" of gay people, and a subsequent kissing incident between Kapoor and Varun Yadav was labelled "assault" by viewers on social media, according to Livemint.

Motiwala has been vocal about queer representation in Indian entertainment. "One story a year, and even that goes to a straight actor — that defeats the whole purpose," he said in a previous interview. Lock Upp Season 2 continues to stream on Netflix.
nri_angle: Motiwala's candid revelations about navigating queer identity within a Muslim family have resonated with diaspora audiences following LGBTQ+ acceptance conversations in Indian communities abroad.
